baslik: 3,000 children in Gaza killed by Israel since Oct. 7: Palestine's UN envoy
metin:
Palestine's UN representative addressed an emergency General Assembly session, stating that approximately 3,000 children have been killed in Gaza since October 7. In an emotional speech, Riyad Mansour declared: "There is no time to mourn, more death is on the way."

According to Mansour, Israeli attacks have resulted in 7,000 Palestinian deaths overall, with women and children comprising roughly 70 percent of casualties. He emphasized the scale of destruction, noting that over 40 percent of Gaza's homes have been destroyed, displacing 1.4 million people.

Mansour also highlighted that approximately 1,600 Palestinians remain trapped under rubble, either killed or injured. He referenced the humanitarian crisis, stating that Israeli Foreign Minister Eli Cohen called for hostage releases while Palestinians have lost homes and families.

The conflict began when Hamas launched Operation Al-Aqsa Flood on October 7, a multi-pronged assault involving rocket fire and infiltrations. Hamas cited the Al-Aqsa Mosque storming and settler violence as motivations. Israel subsequently conducted extensive military operations against Hamas targets throughout Gaza.

The territory's 2.3 million residents face severe shortages of food, water, medicine, and fuel, with humanitarian aid deliveries falling significantly short of actual needs.
